messages.content: Write the invitation copy for a webinar about database performance tuning. Around 200 words.

**Subject: The 12-second query is a red herring**

You know the drill. Open the slow query log, spot the monster, add an index, take a bow. Then p99 hasn't budged an inch.

The thing eating your latency is the 40-millisecond query that fires 4,000 times a minute.

On **[DATE] at [TIME]**, [SPEAKER] shows you how to catch those. Six years keeping a 200-node Postgres fleet upright at [COMPANY]. Ninety minutes, live, on a database you're free to wreck yourself.

What we'll cover:

- Reading EXPLAIN ANALYZE when the plan is lying to you
- The index is right there and the planner still ignores it
- Connection pool sizing: the real arithmetic, so 100 stops being your default
- Catching lock contention before somebody gets paged
- When to quit tuning and just buy the RAM

Bring a plan from your own system. The last twenty minutes belong to whatever lands in the chat, worst one first.

No opening segment on why performance matters. You'd have closed the tab already.

**[Save my seat]** — free, and everyone who registers gets the recording.
Rewrite the text above. Keep the same length and the same purpose. Return only the rewritten text.

output:
**Subject: Stop blaming the 12-second query**

We all know the ritual. Crack open the slow query log, find the beast, throw an index at it, feel good for a day. p99 doesn't move.

What's actually draining you is the 40ms query running 4,000 times a minute.

On **[DATE] at [TIME]**, [SPEAKER] walks through how to find those. Six years keeping a 200-node Postgres fleet from falling over at [COMPANY]. Ninety minutes, live, against a database you can break however you like.

On the agenda:

- Reading EXPLAIN ANALYZE when the plan is telling you lies
- The index exists, the planner won't touch it, and why
- Connection pool sizing: the actual math, so you stop defaulting to 100
- Spotting lock contention before it wakes somebody up at 3am
- Knowing when tuning is done and it's time to buy RAM

Bring a plan from your own database. The final twenty minutes go to whatever shows up in the chat, ugliest one first.

There's no warm-up segment explaining why performance matters. You'd have bailed already.

**[Save my seat]** — free, and registering gets you the recording either way.
